findings.description: On parse-error (action='retain'), the watcher skips mergeAndWrite entirely (flushPending continues past the retain branch and only calls mergeAndWrite if writableUpdates.length > 0). The sidecar's unmatched/unmatchedSummary are never refreshed to include the new 'parse-error' entry, violating plan AC #4 ('After any incremental write, unmatched and unmatchedSummary are structurally equal to a full walkRalphState... covering parse-error'). Prior byTaskId entry is preserved correctly, but the unmatched fragment is dropped.
findings.suggestedFix: When all updates are retain, still invoke mergeAndWrite with the retain updates so unmatched + unmatchedSummary refresh (dropTouchedUnmatched + append unmatchedFragment + re-summarize). Alternatively, in mergeAndWrite, stop short-circuiting on action==='retain' for the unmatched slice — keep skipping byTaskId mutation but still apply the touched/unmatchedFragment refresh and write. Add a regression test that touches a malformed job-state.json and asserts the sidecar's unmatched array contains the parse-error entry within the debounce window.
findings.resolution: flushPending now passes retain updates through mergeAndWrite; mergeAndWrite applies touched+unmatchedFragment refresh even on retain (byTaskId untouched).

findings.sectionRef: plan.md AC Functional - lock metadata process labels
findings.description: Plan AC explicitly enumerates lock metadata process labels as 'standalone' | 'standalone-oneshot' | 'vite-plugin'. The one-shot path in scripts/sync-ralph-state.mjs uses processLabel: 'one-shot' instead of 'standalone-oneshot'. This is a downstream contract divergence — Plan 11's sync.watch_status MCP tool reads the JSON content. CLAUDE.md for this job also asserts 'The lock-file JSON contract { pid, process, startedAt } is consumed by Plans 06 / 08 / 11; do NOT ship a 0-byte sentinel.' The label string is part of that contract.
findings.suggestedFix: Change processLabel: 'one-shot' to processLabel: 'standalone-oneshot' in runOneShot. Update syncRalphStateCli.test.ts assertions accordingly so the canonical fresh-lock diagnostic for one-shot self-contention matches the plan-enumerated label.
findings.resolution: runOneShot now uses processLabel: 'standalone-oneshot' per plan AC enumeration.

findings.description: parseWatchedPath returns undefined for any brainstorm path whose second segment isn't 'brainstorm.json'. A chokidar 'unlinkDir' event for '.ralph/brainstorms/<slug>' arrives with parts === ['<slug>'] (parts[1] === undefined), so brainstorm directory deletions are silently dropped and stale brainstorm-derived entries persist in byTaskId. Plan AC: 'If the slug directory or all bundle files are gone, the affected task entry is removed from byTaskId in the next debounced write' — currently not honored for brainstorms.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow brainstorm enqueue when parts.length === 1 (directory event) OR parts[1] === 'brainstorm.json'. Reject anything else (e.g., 'selected-direction.md' continues to be filtered). Add a unit test that emits unlinkDir for a brainstorm slug and asserts the task entry is removed.
findings.resolution: parseWatchedPath now accepts brainstorm directory-level events (parts.length === 1); only filters parts[1] !== 'brainstorm.json' when nested file events occur.

findings.description: The 'all' event handler is registered before the cold-start walk. After the 'ready' promise resolves but before currentState is assigned, a chokidar event can fire, scheduleFlush() is called, and if debounceMs is small (tests use 10ms) the debounce timer may fire flushPending before line 159 completes. flushPending then calls mergeAndWrite({ currentState: undefined, ... }) which throws ('mergeAndWrite requires repoRoot, config, currentState, and updates') and the queued change is lost (pendingChanges was already cleared). With production debounceMs=2000 this race is unlikely but the failure mode is silent data loss. The plan documents (F-010) the chosen strategy as 'cold-start-then-subscribe-then-rescan'; this code does subscribe-then-cold-start.
findings.suggestedFix: Either (A) defer attaching the 'all' handler until after currentState is assigned and writeSidecar resolves, OR (B) in flushPending, guard with `if (!currentState) { reschedule and return }` so events that race the cold-start are deferred rather than dropped. Option B aligns with strategy (B) in plan F-010 ('cold-start-then-subscribe-then-rescan' / first debounce reconciles).
findings.resolution: Added coldStartReady flag + earlyEventBuffer: events that arrive before currentState is assigned are buffered (not dropped), then drained into pendingChanges and reconciled on the first debounce tick. flushPending also guards on !coldStartReady and reschedules.

findings.description: Plan AC reads: `status` returns `{ running: boolean, pendingSlugs: string[], queueDepth: number, lastTickAt?: string }`. Implementation returns `{ currentState, pendingChanges, consecutiveFailures, stopped }` — different keys, different semantics. PRD US-003 ACs are silent on the exact shape and tests assert the implemented shape, so the build is green, but downstream Plan 11 sync.watch_status (referenced by plan Technical Constraints) expects the documented shape.
findings.suggestedFix: Either (A) rename/extend the status getter to expose `running` (true while !stopped), `pendingSlugs` (kind:slug strings), `queueDepth` (pendingChanges.size), `lastTickAt` (set in flushPending after a successful merge), keeping the current internal fields for tests if needed, OR (B) raise it as a Deferred Question and amend plan.md AC #2 to match what shipped. Picking (A) is straightforward and preserves Plan 11 alignment.
findings.resolution: status object now exposes plan-AC keys (running, pendingSlugs, queueDepth, lastTickAt) alongside legacy keys (currentState, pendingChanges, consecutiveFailures, stopped). lastTickAt is set after each successful merge.

findings.description: deriveAffectedTaskUpdate calls readAllBundles on every invocation. Plan Architecture states it should read 'ONLY the files belonging to those bundles' (the input slug + cross-kind candidates competing for the same taskId). At scale (dozens of jobs + groups + brainstorms), every debounced change re-walks the entire .ralph/ tree synchronously via fs.readdirSync/fs.readFileSync. Correctness is preserved (the resulting fragment is filtered to relevant taskIds), so this is a performance/design concern, not a behavior bug. Compounds with the 30s heartbeat interval and N concurrent jobs writing job-state.json.
findings.suggestedFix: Reshape deriveAffectedTaskUpdate to: (1) read the affected (kind, slug) bundle directly via readBundleForSlug; (2) determine the taskId via resolveTaskIdForSlug + currentState lookup; (3) read cross-kind candidates only for that taskId (job/group/brainstorm slugs that resolve to the same taskId), not the whole tree. Falls back to readAllBundles only when the taskId is ambiguous (no override + no slug match in overview-data).
findings.resolution: Prototyped a collectAffectedBundles per-slug refactor (commit reverted) but it breaks plan AC #4 — orphan slugs newly created during the debounce window need to surface as `no-matching-task-id` unmatched entries, and the only discovery path is a full subdir walk. Added an explicit TODO at deriveAffectedTaskUpdate's full-walk call documenting the limitation and the two follow-up options (track newly-observed slugs via chokidar add/addDir, OR relax AC #4 for the rare new-orphan case). Performance impact remains bounded by the 2s debounce + ignored-pattern filter.

findings.description: matchesIgnored builds a new RegExp from each ignored pattern twice per call (once for `relative`, once for `${relative}/`). For chokidar with `ignored: <function>`, this function is called for every file the watcher considers, potentially thousands of times during startup walks. Compile patterns once at start().
findings.suggestedFix: Precompile config.watcher.ignored into RegExp[] once in start() (or memoize globToRegExp results) and reuse the array in matchesIgnored. Same fix applies to sync-core.mjs:588-601 which has the duplicate implementation; consider moving globToRegExp into a shared helper.
findings.resolution: start() now compiles ignored patterns once via compileIgnoredPatterns and passes RegExp[] into the chokidar ignored callback. matchesIgnored detects pre-compiled RegExp[] and skips re-compilation.

findings.sectionRef: Code duplication between sync-core.mjs and watch-ralph-state.mjs
findings.description: globToRegExp, matchesIgnored, toPosix, splitPath are duplicated verbatim between scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs and scripts/lib/watch-ralph-state.mjs. Both files also define their own resolveHeadShortSha (with watch-ralph-state.mjs duplicating sync-ralph-state.mjs's helper despite plan F-007 explicitly noting start() should reuse the CLI helper).
findings.suggestedFix: Extract a small scripts/lib/path-utils.mjs (or extend resolve-config.mjs) exporting { globToRegExp, matchesIgnored, toPosix, resolveHeadShortSha } and consume from all three callers.
findings.resolution: Added scripts/lib/path-utils.mjs (+ .d.mts) exporting { globToRegExp, compileIgnoredPatterns, matchesIgnored, toPosix, splitPath, resolveHeadShortSha }. sync-core.mjs, watch-ralph-state.mjs, and sync-ralph-state.mjs all consume the shared helpers.

findings.description: isLiveProcess returns `true` on any non-ESRCH error, which includes EPERM. The plan Architecture explicitly calls this out as correct ('treat as alive'). Implementation matches. However, on Windows process.kill(pid, 0) with the wrong-PID-but-valid-user case can return success without throwing — and the catch path only distinguishes ESRCH vs other. If the PID has been recycled and is now owned by a different user, the lock will never be released by liveness probing. Documented residual risk per plan Risk Areas #2; not blocking, but worth a note in the code comment so future maintainers don't shorten the alive branch.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a JSDoc comment above isLiveProcess noting the PID-reuse residual risk and pointing to plan.md Risk Areas #2. No code change required.
findings.resolution: Added JSDoc to isLiveProcess explaining the zero-signal probe semantics, why EPERM is treated as alive (conservative), and the PID-reuse residual risk on Windows + general OS-level.

findings.description: flushPending wraps the entire body in try/catch and routes errors to onError. When mergeAndWrite throws (e.g., disk full, EBUSY past retry limit), the cleared pendingChanges entries are lost — they were drained into `changes` at line 68-69 before the try block. Subsequent .ralph/ activity will still trigger writes, but the specific changes that failed are silently dropped.
findings.suggestedFix: On catch, re-enqueue the failed `changes` back into pendingChanges and call scheduleFlush() so the next debounce retries. Cap retries (e.g., 3) to avoid an infinite loop on persistent disk-full conditions; after the cap, drop with a stderr warning.
findings.resolution: flushPending catch block now re-enqueues failed changes into pendingChanges and calls scheduleFlush(); per-(kind,slug) retry counter capped at MAX_FLUSH_RETRIES=3, after which the change is dropped with a stderr warning. Successful flush resets the retry counter.

findings.description: `scripts/lib/watch-ralph-state.mjs:35-48` and `scripts/lib/watch-ralph-state.d.mts:15-19`: the watcher does not export the planned `status()` API or the required `{ running, pendingSlugs, queueDepth, lastTickAt }` shape. It exposes a `status` object with different fields, so the debug/future-MCP acceptance criterion is not met.
findings.resolution: Same fix as F-005: status object + .d.mts now expose running/pendingSlugs/queueDepth/lastTickAt alongside legacy keys.

findings.description: `scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs:158-163`: `deriveAffectedTaskUpdate` calls `readAllBundles(...)` on every file change. The plan explicitly requires per-slug derivation that reads only touched/cross-kind candidate bundles; this implementation degenerates to a full Ralph walk per debounce tick.
findings.resolution: Same as F-006: per-slug refactor breaks AC #4 for newly-observed orphan slugs. Deferred to a follow-up plan; TODO comment added at the call site.

findings.description: `scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs:220-234` and `scripts/lib/watch-ralph-state.mjs:77-94`: `retain` updates are discarded before unmatched refresh, so malformed changed bundles never update `unmatched` / `unmatchedSummary` with `parse-error`. This violates the merge invariant requiring parse-error unmatched slices to match the fresh derivation while preserving prior `byTaskId`.
findings.resolution: Same fix as F-001: retain updates flow through mergeAndWrite; the unmatched slice gets refreshed (drop touched + append unmatchedFragment + re-sort + re-summarize) while byTaskId is left untouched on retain.

findings.description: `scripts/lib/watch-ralph-state.mjs:179-187`: brainstorm directory deletions are ignored unless the event path is exactly `<slug>/brainstorm.json`. A chokidar `unlinkDir` for `.ralph/brainstorms/<slug>` will not enqueue removal, leaving stale brainstorm-derived task state despite the plan’s deletion/removal criterion.
findings.resolution: Same fix as F-003: parseWatchedPath now accepts directory-level brainstorm events and filters nested non-brainstorm.json files instead.

findings.description: `scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs:339-440` defines `collectAffectedBundles` which is never called anywhere in the worktree (`grep collectAffectedBundles` returns only its definition). This is the prototype that F-006/F-012's wontfix resolution describes as 'reverted', but the function body is still left behind in the file — ~100 lines of dead code with non-trivial control flow (taskId resolution, slugsByKind iteration, three readJobLikeBundles / readBrainstormBundles calls). Falls under the reviewer rubric's 'Dead code — unreachable branches / commented-out blocks / unused imports/variables'.
findings.suggestedFix: Delete the `collectAffectedBundles` function. If keeping it as a reference for the future-plan refactor described in the F-006 resolution is desired, move it to a comment or to plan.md / a follow-up issue rather than leaving live (uncalled) source code in sync-core.mjs. The existing TODO at line 162-172 already documents the deferred refactor.
findings.resolution: Deleted collectAffectedBundles (~100 lines of dead code). The F-006 deferred-refactor TODO at deriveAffectedTaskUpdate's full-walk call remains as the canonical reference for the future per-slug refactor; no orphaned helpers since loadOverviewData/findCurrentTaskIdForSlug/slugFromArtifact/readJobLikeBundles/readBrainstormBundles are still consumed elsewhere.

findings.description: `scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs:146` calls `readBundleForSlug({ ... kind, slug })` and uses the result only for the `directBundle?.parseError` branch at line 150. The non-parse-error path proceeds to `readAllBundles(...)` at line 174, which re-reads the same bundle (and every other bundle). For the parse-error path this is correct, but for the common upsert/remove path the directBundle read is wasted work (one extra fs.readdirSync + fs.readFileSync for the slug). Severity Low because correctness is preserved and F-006 already documents the broader per-slug refactor as deferred.
findings.suggestedFix: Either (a) defer the `readBundleForSlug` call until after the parse-error branch is known to be needed (read it lazily inside the if block; on the upsert path, look up the bundle in `fragment.byTaskId` or skip entirely), or (b) thread `directBundle` into the assembleStateFromBundles call so the duplicate read is avoided. Lowest-touch fix: move the readBundleForSlug call to happen only when the early-return parse-error path is taken. Wait until F-006's full per-slug refactor lands and roll this into it.
findings.resolution: Dropped the readBundleForSlug call (option a). readAllBundles is invoked once and its result is reused — parse-error detection now finds the (kind, slug) bundle in the existing array, and the non-parse-error path reuses the same bundles for assembleStateFromBundles. Saves one fs.readdirSync + fs.readFileSync per debounce tick; existing parse-error retain test (syncCore.test.ts:239) continues to pass.

findings.sectionRef: ralphWatcher.test.ts regression coverage for round-1 fixes
findings.description: Round-1 resolutions for F-001 (retain → unmatched refresh), F-003/F-014 (brainstorm unlinkDir directory-level event), F-004 (cold-start race / earlyEventBuffer), and F-010 (flush retry counter + drop-after-3) explicitly recommended new regression tests, but none were added in iteration 1 or 2. `tools/overview-viewer/src/__tests__/ralphWatcher.test.ts` lacks: (a) an assertion that after the watcher processes a malformed job-state.json change, the persisted sidecar's `unmatched` array contains the `parse-error` entry for that slug (the current retains-malformed test only asserts the stderr log + counter, not the on-disk sidecar slice); (b) a brainstorm-slug `unlinkDir` test that emits `unlinkDir .ralph/brainstorms/<slug>` and asserts the affected task entry is removed; (c) a cold-start race test that fires a chokidar 'all' event between the 'ready' resolution and the writeSidecar await, then verifies the early event is drained into the first debounce (no thrown 'mergeAndWrite requires currentState'); (d) an EBUSY/disk-full simulation that forces mergeAndWrite to reject three times for the same (kind,slug) and asserts the watcher emits 'dropping <kind>/<slug> after 3 failed flush attempts'. Without these tests, a future refactor of flushPending or parseWatchedPath could silently regress all four fixes — the existing tests pass against both the buggy and the fixed code. Severity Medium because the fixes themselves are correct and verified by code inspection, but the durability of the contract is unguarded.
findings.suggestedFix: Add four tests under `describe('ralph watcher', ...)`: (1) 'refreshes sidecar unmatched on malformed JSON retain' — write valid job-state.json, await start, then write malformed JSON, emit 'change', advance fake timers past debounce, read overview-ralph-state.json from disk, assert `unmatched` contains `{ kind: 'job', slug: '<test>', reason: 'parse-error' }` AND byTaskId entry for the slug is preserved (F-001/F-013); (2) 'removes a task when a brainstorm slug directory is unlinked' — pre-populate a brainstorm bundle, await start, emit `unlinkDir .ralph/brainstorms/<slug>`, advance timers, assert byTaskId[<id>] is removed (F-003/F-014); (3) 'buffers early chokidar events until cold-start completes' — schedule an emit('all', 'change', ...) inside a microtask between watcher.emit('ready') and the test's flush-timer advance, assert the change still produces a sidecar write on the first debounce and no error is propagated to onError (F-004); (4) 'drops persistent flush failures after MAX_FLUSH_RETRIES' — stub `mergeAndWrite` to reject 4 times, emit a single change, advance debounce three times, assert `onError` fires three times AND the fourth tick emits `'dropping job/<slug> after 3 failed flush attempts'` to stderr (F-010). All four can reuse the existing fake-watcher + fake-timer harness in this test file. The F-010 test in particular guards against the silent-data-loss failure mode the original finding warned about.
findings.resolution: Added 5 regression tests to tools/overview-viewer/src/__tests__/ralphWatcher.test.ts: (1) malformed JSON retain refreshes sidecar unmatched parse-error entry while byTaskId is preserved (F-001/F-013); (2) brainstorm slug-directory unlinkDir removes byTaskId entry (F-003/F-014); (3) chokidar 'all' event raced against cold-start is buffered and replayed on first debounce with no onError (F-004); (4) persistent mergeAndWrite failure drops change after MAX_FLUSH_RETRIES=3 with stderr warning; (5) bonus transient-failure recovery within the retry cap (F-010). Pre-existing syncLock 'touch refreshes mtime' flake is unrelated (verified by stashing F-017 changes and reproducing the failure).
